defect.problem: The holding states Eatherton 'retains controlling force notwithstanding the Supreme Court's intervening decisions in Gant and Riley.' But the opinion is unambiguous that the two intervening precedents Perez relied on were Chadwick and Gant, not Riley. Riley was not part of Perez's challenge; the majority invoked Riley AFFIRMATIVELY to support Eatherton's survival (showing Gant is vehicle-limited and Robinson survived Chadwick). Chadwick — which the court analyzes in its own section (C.1) as one of the two 'relevant intervening Supreme Court precedents' — is omitted from the holding entirely and silently replaced by Riley, inverting Riley's role and misstating the doctrinal frame.
defect.proposed_fix: Change 'intervening decisions in Gant and Riley' to 'intervening decisions in Chadwick and Gant' in the holding (and correspondingly in Background/Issue/Rule/Application). If Riley is retained, describe it as authority the majority used to support Eatherton, not as a challenge Eatherton had to overcome.
defect.evidence_quote: The post-Eatherton developments that Perez has in mind are two Supreme Court precedents: Chadwick and Gant.
defect.locator_note: frontmatter 'holding' field — phrase 'notwithstanding the Supreme Court's intervening decisions in Gant and Riley'; contradicted at slip op. pp. 6, 16, and 31-32 ('the relevant intervening Supreme Court precedents are Chadwick and Gant').

Opinion p.1: 'Because the use of an LPR did not constitute a search, no warrant was required; the stop was supported by reasonable suspicion, and the officer found the Glock and its machinegun conversion switch in plain view. Section III.A holds LPR use did not invade a reasonable expectation of privacy and was no search; Section III.B.1 holds the stop was supported by reasonable suspicion; III.B.2.a upholds the plain-view seizure of the Glock and switch; Section V holds circuit precedent (Hollis/Wilson) forecloses the § 922(o) Second Amendment challenge; disposition AFFIRMED.
Charge was 18 U.S.C. § 922(o) machinegun possession; conviction affirmed — 'machinegun conviction was affirmed' is accurate.
residual_risks: The firearm was physically retrieved during an inventory search, but the court affirmed on plain view (upholding the district court's plain-view determination), so 'lawfully seized ... in plain view' tracks the court's rationale.
